text.p: Globalisation of world trade will force advertising agencies to rethink strategies and incorporate more regional culture into international brand management, the chairman of a top French agency said on Tuesday.
"The problem today is how to be well-rooted in any particular country, any history, any culture and be part of the future," Maurice Levy, chairman of Publicis SA, told Reuters in an interview.
Levy said increasingly global brand awareness gave the advertising industry a major headache in projecting brands in the most positive ways in different regions of the world.
"The brand is becoming more and more important -- it is the major asset for the client," said Levy.

Levy, in Singapore to sign a deal taking a 60 percent stake in local advertising agency Eureka as part of a US$250 million global acquisitions strategy, said fears that globalisation would lead to a bland Westernisation of Asian culture were unfounded.
"My feeling is that the more we go towards globalisation, the more people need to have roots," he said.

"Globalisation doesn't mean necessarily that you would have the same campaign everywhere. Globalisation means that the culture, the TV, the people (of different countries) can have a fantastic exchange to enrich themselves."

Levy said Publicis's acquisition plans would respond to international clients' needs for advertising agencies with global reach but with good local feel to project brands in the best way at the national level.

Describing Asia as "a reservoir for growth for the next 30 years" for world trade, including advertising revenue, Levy said the region would provide up to 10 percent of Publicis' projected billing revenues of US$6.0 billion by 2000.
He said Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines offered interesting opportunities along with China, the region's expected economic engine in the next century.
